title: A Rule Before the Notice
fact_notes: 架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査、統計、法令、医療制度、実証結果ではない。登録台帳は制作来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A fictional town introduces a new rule restricting the use of a public square during certain hours of the evening.
sentences.ja: 架空の町は夜間の特定時間に公共広場の利用を制限する新規則を導入する。

sentences.en: Officials publish the announcement on the town's website and assume that residents will become familiar with the restriction before it takes effect.
sentences.ja: 職員は町のサイトで告知し施行前に住民が制限を知ると想定する。

sentences.en: Several days after the change, however, a visitor arrives at the square without knowing that its permitted hours have been reduced.
sentences.ja: 変更数日後、許可時間が短縮されたと知らず来場者が広場に来る。

sentences.en: The incident encourages the council to examine the difference between making information publicly available and ensuring that people have a reasonable opportunity to encounter it.
sentences.ja: この出来事は情報を公開することと人々が合理的に情報に触れる機会を確保することの違いを調べるよう議会を促す。

sentences.en: Some residents regularly consult the town's website because it provides details about local services.
sentences.ja: 地域サービスの詳細が載っているので定期的に町のサイトを見る住民もいる。

sentences.en: Others visit the square only occasionally and may have no particular reason to search for a recent change in its opening hours.
sentences.ja: 一方広場を時折訪れるだけで開場時間の最近の変更を検索する特別な理由がない人もいる。

sentences.en: The council recognizes that information can remain effectively invisible to its intended audience even when no technical restriction prevents access to the published material.
sentences.ja: 技術的なアクセス制限がなくても対象読者に情報が実質的に見えないままとなることがあると認識する。

sentences.en: A procedure intended to communicate new responsibilities may therefore require more than providing a document at a location known mainly to regular users.
sentences.ja: 新しい責任を伝える手順には常連利用者に主に知られる場所に文書を置く以上のことが必要かもしれない。

sentences.en: The officials consider attaching clear signs at the entrances to the square before the planned change begins.
sentences.ja: 職員は計画変更開始前に広場入口に明確な標識を付けることを検討する。

sentences.en: The signs would identify the relevant hours, explain when the rule becomes effective, and provide a way to obtain further information.
sentences.ja: 標識は関連時間、施行時期、追加情報取得方法を示す。

sentences.en: The council also discusses an introductory period during which staff would explain the new arrangement rather than immediately treating every misunderstanding in the same manner.
sentences.ja: 全ての誤解を即座に同様に扱わず職員が仕組みを説明する導入期間も議論する。

sentences.en: The fictional discussion does not establish what penalties or legal procedures would be appropriate under any actual law.
sentences.ja: 架空の議論は実際の法律下でどの罰則や法的手順が適切か確定しない。

sentences.en: One official raises a concern that signs alone may not communicate every detail of a complicated regulation.
sentences.ja: 標識だけで複雑な規則の全詳細は伝えられないかもしれないと職員が懸念する。

sentences.en: The council consequently separates information necessary for ordinary visitors from additional explanations that people can consult when particular questions arise.
sentences.ja: そこで一般来場者に必要な情報と特定の問いが生じた時参照できる追加説明を分ける。

sentences.en: It avoids promising that every person will notice every announcement, recognizing that even carefully designed communication has limitations.
sentences.ja: 慎重な伝達にも限界があると認識し全員が全告知に気づくとは約束しない。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the officials can examine whether the available channels are reasonably connected to the situations in which people need the information.
sentences.ja: それでも利用できる伝達経路が情報を必要とする状況に合理的に結びつくか調べられる。

sentences.en: A public announcement serves its purpose through the opportunities it creates for people to understand a change, not merely through the existence of a published document.
sentences.ja: 公共告知は文書公開の存在だけでなく変更を理解する機会を作ることで目的を果たす。

sentences.en: People cannot reliably adjust their behavior to responsibilities whose existence they have had little opportunity to discover.
sentences.ja: 存在を知る機会がほとんどなかった責任に合わせて確実に行動を調整することはできない。

sentences.en: The example illustrates why evaluating the accessibility of information requires attention to the circumstances in which its intended recipients encounter it.
sentences.ja: 情報の利用しやすさの評価には対象受取人が情報に出会う事情への注意が必要な理由を例は示す。

sentences.en: Making a rule visible can be an important part of making it meaningful in everyday public life.
sentences.ja: 規則を見えるようにすることは日常の公共生活で意味あるものにする重要な一部になり得る。

vocabulary.definition: in a way accessible to the public
quality of being easy to reach

questions.prompt: What does the new rule restrict?
options: All access to the town website.
Use of a public square at certain evening hours.

questions.prompt: What did the visitor's experience reveal?
options: Everyone knew the rule before it began.
The visitor had deliberately ignored a notice.
Information publication does not guarantee awareness.

questions.prompt: Why do some residents consult the website regularly?
options: They are required to visit every hour.
They must book the square daily.
It is the only place to meet neighbors.

questions.prompt: Why may occasional visitors miss the change?
options: They may have no reason to search for new hours.
They are prohibited from reading the site.
They always know when rules change.

questions.prompt: What is proposed at the square?
options: A new building on the square.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the introductory period?
options: Guarantee a fixed penalty for every visitor.
Allow staff to explain the new arrangement.
Remove the rule before it starts.

questions.prompt: What distinction does the council make about information?
options: Essential visitor information and further details.
Every person will notice every sign.
Signs can contain every possible detail.
Even carefully designed communication has limitations.
Published rules need no other communication.
Public information must be accessible where people reasonably need it.
Publishing a rule always ensures awareness.
Signs are the only valid legal notice.
Every misunderstanding should receive identical penalties.

paraphrases.source: The council recognizes that information can remain effectively invisible to its intended audience even when no technical restriction prevents access to the published material.
paraphrases.rewrite: Information may be unnoticed despite being technically accessible.

paraphrases.source: The council also discusses an introductory period during which staff would explain the new arrangement rather than immediately treating every misunderstanding in the same manner.
paraphrases.rewrite: They consider a transition period for explaining the rule.
